text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- MARKET SEES PREMIUM OF UP TO 30 PCT IN CVRD SALE

Two consortia, one led by the Votorantim industrial group and another led by steelmaker CSN, will bid at the April 29 privatization auction of Brazil's state miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce. Market analysts expect CVRD to be sold at a premium of between 20 percent and 30 percent over the firm's base price.
-- IMF WANTS BRAZIL TO SLOW DOWN ECONOMY
International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing-director Michel Camdessus Thursday suggested Brazil should put a brake on the economy in a bid to slow down a widening trade deficit.
-- PROEX EXPORT PROGRAM ALTERED TO BOOST EXPORTS
The Brazilian government simplified some of the conditions for access to export financing under its so-called Proex export program in a move to reduce the country's trade deficit.
-- MINIMUM WAGE LIKELY TO RISE TO 120 REAIS
Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan is likely to announce today a 7.14 percent rise in the country's minimum wage to 120 reais from 112 reais.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said in Canada the Chamber of Deputies' decision to reject an amendment to the government's civil service reform bill was "cranky."
-- GOVERNMENT, CONGRESS CLASH ON REFORM, BOND PROBE

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso Thursday criticized Congressmen for rejecting an amendment to the government's administrative reform. He attacked the opposition and said it was shameful it took lawmakers two years to vote on the reforms.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
